rubric.why: Identifies the subject studied in molecular biology.
rubric.description: States that molecular biology studies biological molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying biological molecules as its subject.

rubric.why: Shows that biological processes are studied at the molecular level.
rubric.description: States that it studies biological processes at the molecular level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the molecular level.

modelAnswer: Molecular biology is the branch of biology that studies biological molecules.
It examines biological processes at the molecular level.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell membrane according to the fluid mosaic model.

rubric.why: The model describes the membrane as a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.description: Names the basic phospholipid bilayer structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the phospholipid bilayer.

rubric.why: Proteins contribute to the mosaic appearance, while movement of membrane components makes it fluid.
rubric.description: Describes proteins embedded in the bilayer or the movement that makes it fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning embedded proteins or movement of membrane components.

modelAnswer: According to the fluid mosaic model, the cell membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer.
Proteins are embedded in the bilayer, and its components can move, making the membrane fluid and mosaic in appearance.

items.followUp: Write the taxonomic categories in order from kingdom to species.

rubric.why: A taxonomic hierarchy is an ordered arrangement used in classification.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomic hierarchy as an orderly arrangement of organisms or categories.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that organisms or categories are arranged in an order.

accept: species genus family order class phylum kingdom
rubric.why: The sequence gives the main taxonomic ranks from lower to higher.
rubric.description: Gives the sequence of ranks from species to kingdom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct sequence from species through kingdom.

modelAnswer: Taxonomic hierarchy is the orderly arrangement of organisms into taxonomic categories from lower to higher ranks.
The main sequence is species genus family order class phylum kingdom.

items.followUp: What is a species? Give one example of a species.

rubric.why: A taxon is a group of organisms classified at a particular taxonomic rank.
rubric.description: Defines a taxon as a group of organisms at a taxonomic rank.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a taxon as a group of organisms or a taxonomic rank.

rubric.why: Species is a valid example of a taxon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid example, such as species.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a group of organisms at a particular taxonomic rank in biological classification.
Species is one example of a taxon.

rubric.why: Mitosis involves one division of the nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies mitosis as division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nucleus divides.

accept: same chromosome number as the parent cell
rubric.why: Mitosis produces two identical daughter cells that retain the parent cell's chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two genetically identical daughter cells are produced, or that they retain the parent's chromosome number.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is the division of the nucleus once.
It produces two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same chromosome number as the parent cell.

items.followUp: Explain the role of photosystem II and photosystem I in non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

rubric.why: The Z scheme represents electron movement during non-cyclic photophosphorylation, from water towards NADP.
rubric.description: Identifies the Z scheme as an electron pathway in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying electron flow or the transfer of electrons from water to NADP.

rubric.why: The pathway involves photosystems II and I and has a characteristic Z-shaped pattern.
rubric.description: Mentions both photosystems or the characteristic Z shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both photosystems or describing the Z-shaped pattern.

modelAnswer: The Z scheme shows electron flow during non-cyclic photophosphorylation from water through photosystem II and photosystem I to NADP.
The changes in electron energy along this pathway form a Z-shaped pattern.
